This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `find_adt_field`, `field_ty`, `write_field_index`, `ban_private_field_access`, and `ban_nonexisting_field`.

When the base type is an `impl Future`, checks whether the requested field exists on the future's `Output` type and, if so, suggests inserting `.await`; otherwise it just labels the field as unknown. It does not call other listed methods.

Builds and emits the main diagnostic for accessing a nonexistent field, specializing suggestions for arrays, raw pointers, type parameters, and opaque futures, then trying a method-call suggestion if calling the base expression would yield a type with the requested field, and adding the Rust-2018 `.await` note when relevant. This method calls the listed methods `no_such_field_err`, `maybe_suggest_array_indexing`, `suggest_first_deref_field`, `point_at_param_definition`, and `suggest_await_on_field_access`.

Emits the private-field-access diagnostic and, when appropriate, suggests calling an accessible method with the same name instead of reading the field. This method calls the listed method `private_field_err`.

Reports the error for treating a method as a field value, then suggests either removing wrapping parentheses for an accidental call pattern, adding call parentheses, or dereferencing first for raw-pointer-to-ADT cases where the field exists after dereference. It does not call other listed methods.

Augments a diagnostic for field access on a type parameter by locating the non-synthetic type parameter declaration in the current body and labeling where that parameter was introduced. It does not call other listed methods.

Produces diagnostics for an unknown field on a struct-like ADT: it first calls `suggest_field_name` to offer a similar field name, and if none is found, it labels the access and lists available fields using `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.

For mistaken tuple-style field syntax on arrays, labels the field as unknown and, when the field parses as an integer and the array length is evaluable, suggests rewriting `.n` as `[n]` with an applicability tuned by bounds confidence. It does not call other listed methods.
For raw-pointer field access, labels the field as unknown and suggests wrapping the base expression in an explicit dereference before accessing the field. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the base `no field` diagnostic and enriches it with suggestions for nested-field access paths, misspelled field names, and visible candidate field listings; it also unwraps `Option`/`Result`-like outer types when searching for nested matches. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy`, `check_for_nested_field_satisfying`, and `name_series_display`.

Autodereferences a base type and gathers visible, suggestable fields from non-enum ADTs, skipping wrappers whose fields are all private and capping the number of searched fields for compile-time cost. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.

Recursively searches through visible nested ADT fields up to depth three for a field satisfying the provided predicate, extending and returning the field path on success. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy` and `check_for_nested_field_satisfying` recursively.

Type-checks indexing expressions by checking both operands, resolving the base type, using normal indexing lookup when available, coercing the index to the required index type and retargeting obligation spans, otherwise probing for a nearly applicable `Index` impl with unsatisfied predicates, and finally emitting specialized diagnostics for non-indexable types such as tuples or pointers. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `lookup_indexing`, `point_at_index`, and `find_and_report_unsatisfied_index_impl`.
Scans fulfillment errors for `SliceIndex` trait obligations and, when found, rewrites their cause span to the provided span so indexing-related diagnostics point at the expression location.

Checks a `yield` expression against the current coroutine context. If coroutine types are available, it calls `check_expr_coercible_to_type` to coerce the yielded value to the coroutine's `yield_ty` and returns the coroutine `resume_ty`. Otherwise it emits an error through `dcx().emit_err`, calls `check_expr` on the yielded value to ensure it is still type-checked, and returns `unit`.

Checks one inline-assembly operand, using `check_expr_with_needs` to type-check the expression with either no place requirement for inputs or mutable-place requirement for outputs, then `require_type_is_sized` to enforce `Sized`. For non-inputs it rejects non-place expressions via `dcx().struct_span_err(...).emit()`. For inputs it calls `structurally_resolve_type` and, when the resolved type is a function item or reference, uses `demand_coerce` to coerce it respectively to a function pointer or raw pointer.

Checks an entire inline `asm!` expression and determines whether it yields `!` or `()`. It calls `check_expr_asm_operand` for each input/output operand, and for label operands it calls `check_block_with_expected` with unit expectation, then uses `demand_suptype` to require `()` when the label block does not diverge. It also restores divergence tracking for label blocks and returns `never` if the asm is guaranteed not to return, otherwise `unit`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/error_rep: Returns whether this diagnostic payload can be enriched with extra naming information; it suppresses extra info for anonymous inferred type placeholders named `_`.

Classifies how to describe the unresolved argument inside another type for diagnostics, returning empty text for inferred/numeric types, `underscore` for `_`, and `has_name` otherwise. This method calls `Ty::is_ty_or_numeric_infer`.

Builds an `InferenceBadError` fallback diagnostic payload from the stored inference metadata, including parent naming details and prefix text. This method calls `InferenceDiagnosticsData::can_add_more_info` and `UnderspecifiedArgKind::try_get_prefix`.
Constructs parent-item diagnostic metadata for a `DefId` by extracting the parent item's display name and descriptive prefix from the type context.

Looks up the parent of a definition and reuses `InferenceDiagnosticsParentData::for_parent_def_id` to build its diagnostic metadata. This method calls `InferenceDiagnosticsParentData::for_parent_def_id`.
Converts an underspecified argument kind into the string diagnostic argument expected by localized error messages, distinguishing type, const, and const-parameter cases.
Returns the printable prefix for underspecified type arguments and `None` for const arguments.
Creates a `FmtPrinter` configured to print unresolved types and consts with user-friendly inferred-variable names, recovering generic parameter names when possible from inference origins.

Formats a type into a diagnostic-friendly string, using function-signature syntax for `fn` items, `Vec<_>` for unresolved `collect` results, and placeholder text for other unresolved inferred types. This function calls `fmt_printer`.
Formats a closure type as `fn(args) -> ret` for diagnostics by extracting its signature and rendering each argument and the return type. This function calls `ty_to_string`.

Extracts the best available diagnostic metadata for an unresolved generic argument, including its displayed name, source span, kind, and optional parent item, with special handling for type and const parameter inference variables. This method calls `InferenceDiagnosticsParentData::for_def_id` when the unresolved argument comes from a named generic parameter.

Builds the fallback inference-failure diagnostic when no better source location can be found, selecting the concrete error struct from the requested error code. This method calls `InferenceDiagnosticsData::make_bad_error`.

Produces the full user-facing inference failure diagnostic by resolving the target argument, extracting its metadata, searching the body for the best annotation source, and then assembling labels and suggestions tailored to let bindings, closure arguments/returns, generic arguments, and method calls. This method calls `InferCtxt::extract_inference_diagnostics_data`, `InferCtxt::bad_inference_failure_err`, `FindInferSourceVisitor::new`, `InferSourceKind::ty_localized_msg`, `InferenceDiagnosticsData::where_x_is_kind`, `UnderspecifiedArgKind::try_get_prefix`, `ty_to_string`, `InferenceDiagnosticsParentData::for_parent_def_id`, and `fmt_printer`.
Returns whether the inferred source or any of its relevant insertion/wrapping spans originated from macro expansion, so such sources can be deprioritized or ignored.

Classifies an inference source for localized messaging and, when possible, provides a printable type description; closure sources are rendered as function signatures and non-inferred concrete types use normal type formatting. This method calls `closure_as_fn_str` and `ty_to_string`.
Initializes a visitor that searches a body for the most useful source location and context to explain an unresolved inference variable.

Computes a heuristic cost for a candidate inference source so the visitor can prefer simpler, clearer annotation sites; it delegates per-argument and per-type scoring to `CostCtxt`. This method calls `CostCtxt::ty_cost` and `CostCtxt::arg_cost`.
Assigns a heuristic complexity cost to a generic argument, treating lifetimes as free, consts as a small fixed cost, and types via `CostCtxt::ty_cost`. This method calls `CostCtxt::ty_cost`.

Assigns a heuristic complexity cost to a type, heavily penalizing closures and function defs while recursively summing the costs of generic arguments and nested component types. This method calls `CostCtxt::arg_cost` and recursively calls `CostCtxt::ty_cost`.

Filters out macro-generated candidates, computes their ranking, applies a special-case improvement for `let x = iter.collect()`-style bindings, and keeps the best inference source seen so far. This method calls `InferSource::from_expansion` and `FindInferSourceVisitor::source_cost`.
Fetches the resolved type of an HIR node from typeck results and resolves any remaining inference variables.
Checks whether a generic argument is the exact unresolved target or is unioned/unified with it through type or const inference equivalence classes.

Walks a generic argument tree to determine whether it contains the unresolved target anywhere inside it, skipping opaque, closure/coroutine, and unevaluated-const subtrees that users cannot name directly. This method calls `FindInferSourceVisitor::generic_arg_is_target`.
Returns the HIR map used by the visitor for nested traversal.

Visits a local binding, recursively walks its contents, and records the binding as a candidate inference source when its inferred type contains the unresolved target and the binding lacks an explicit type annotation. This method calls `FindInferSourceVisitor::opt_node_type`, `FindInferSourceVisitor::generic_arg_contains_target`, and `FindInferSourceVisitor::update_infer_source`.

Visits a body to find closure parameters whose types are inferred and contain the target unresolved generic argument. It calls `opt_node_type` to obtain each parameter’s type, `generic_arg_contains_target` to test whether that type references the target, `update_infer_source` to record a `ClosureArg` inference source when it does, uses `shrink_to_hi` to choose the insertion point for an annotation, and finally calls `walk_body` to continue visiting nested HIR.

Visits expressions to locate the most specific source of missing type information. For call expressions, it explicitly calls `visit_expr` on arguments before the callee, and otherwise delegates traversal to `walk_expr`. It then calls `expr_inferred_arg_iter` to inspect inferred generic arguments on the expression, `generics_of` to fetch the owning generics, `generic_arg_contains_target` to find the unresolved argument, `resolve_vars_if_possible` to normalize arguments, and `update_infer_source` to record a `GenericArg` source with the correct insertion span. Finally, it calls `opt_node_type` to inspect the expression type and, for closures, checks whether the closure output contains the target so it can report the closure return position as another candidate inference source.
Converts a `TypeAnnotationNeeded` variant into the corresponding `rustc_errors::DiagnosticId` by matching `E0282`, `E0283`, or `E0284`. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Builds the generator-specific missing-type-information diagnostic by first resolving inference variables, then extracting inference diagnostic metadata, and finally packaging that into a `NeedTypeInfoInGenerator` diagnostic. It explicitly calls `extract_inference_diagnostics_data` from the Methods List.

Converts a `hir::GeneratorKind` wrapper into a diagnostic string argument such as `async_block`, `async_closure`, `async_fn`, or `generator`. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Fetches the substitutions recorded for a HIR node and resolves any remaining inference variables before returning them. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Examines an expression shape to find candidate generic-argument insertion points for inferred substitutions, covering paths, structs, and method calls. It explicitly calls `node_substs_opt`, `path_inferred_subst_iter`, and `resolved_path_inferred_subst_iter` from the Methods List.

Produces insertion-point candidates for a resolved path by inspecting the path’s own generics and each segment’s generics, while tracking whether a turbofish is already present and skipping `impl Trait` cases. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Computes candidate inferred-substitution insertion points for a `QPath`, delegating resolved paths directly and handling type-relative paths by consulting the type-dependent def, segment generics, and parent item context. It explicitly calls `resolved_path_inferred_subst_iter` from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/astconv/: Builds and emits the E0747 diagnostic when a supplied generic argument has the wrong kind for a parameter, adding targeted suggestions for const/type confusion, missing braces around const args, `_` const inference, and possible ordering mistakes. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Constructs the final substitution list for a definition and all of its generic parents by walking the parent chain, reusing parent substitutions, inserting `Self` when needed, consuming explicit path arguments, and synthesizing inferred arguments through the context object in parameter order. It calls `generic_arg_mismatch_err` from the Methods List to report argument-kind mismatches while assembling substitutions.

Convenience entry point for call syntax that normalizes missing path arguments, determines whether the call is a method or value position, computes whether `Self` is implicit, and then delegates generic-argument count validation. It calls `check_generic_arg_count` from the Methods List.

Validates explicit generic arguments against a definition’s generic parameters by computing expected counts, rejecting illegal associated-type bindings outside type position, checking explicit late-bound lifetimes, separating lifetime checks from type/const checks, and emitting structured diagnostics for wrong counts or misplaced arguments. It calls `prohibit_assoc_ty_binding` and `prohibit_explicit_late_bound_lifetimes` from the Methods List.
Emits the `AssocTypeBindingNotAllowed` error for an associated-type binding used in a disallowed position. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Detects and reports explicit lifetime arguments when late-bound lifetime parameters are present, either as a hard error or a lint depending on call position and argument counts, and returns whether such late-bound lifetimes were encountered. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Main entry point for const-evaluatability checking. It expands abstract consts with `expand_abstract_consts`, inspects the result via `kind`, and immediately accepts trivial const kinds or rejects `Infer`. When `generic_const_exprs` is enabled, it re-expands the const, checks whether an unevaluated const is an anon const via `def_kind`, and for non-anon consts calls `satisfied_from_param_env`; if that fails, it uses `has_non_region_infer` and `has_non_region_param` to classify the failure. As a fallback for unevaluated consts, it calls `const_eval_resolve` to actually evaluate the const and maps evaluation errors into `NotConstEvaluatable`, while unsupported `ConstKind::Expr` triggers compiler bugs/diagnostics.

Checks whether a const can be justified by `ConstEvaluatable` predicates in the parameter environment. It iterates over `caller_bounds`, filters `ConstEvaluatable` clauses through `kind` and `skip_binder`, expands each candidate with `expand_abstract_consts`, and visits the candidate const tree with `visit_with`. During that traversal it relies on `visit_const` to test whether the queried const matches a predicate or one of its abstract-const subexpressions, and accepts only a unique successful match.

Visits a constant candidate while searching for a unique `ConstEvaluatable` match from the parameter environment. It uses `probe`, `new_in_snapshot`, `eq`, `dummy`, `ty`, `is_ok`, `select_all_or_error`, and `is_empty` to test whether the visited const is equal in both type and value to the target const under the current obligation context, updating `single_match` only when the match is unique. If the const is an expression (`kind` / `Expr`), it recursively visits sub-consts by calling `visit_with`, otherwise it returns `Continue`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::d: Destructures a fully evaluated `ty::ConstKind::Value` aggregate into a `ty::DestructuredConst` by matching the constant type and rebuilding each field element with `tcx.mk_const`; for ADTs it also computes the active variant index from the `ValTree` and collects per-field constants.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::c: Returns whether a MIR binary operator is permitted in abstract consts, accepting arithmetic/bitwise/shift/comparison ops and rejecting `Offset`. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Returns whether a MIR unary operator is permitted in abstract consts, allowing only `Not` and `Neg`. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::r: Recursively lowers a THIR expression into a type-level abstract constant, handling literals, named consts, const params, calls, casts, and supported unary/binary forms while emitting `GenericConstantTooComplex` diagnostics for unsupported constructs. This method calls `recurse_build` recursively to lower subexpressions, calls `check_binop` and `check_unop` to validate operators, and calls `maybe_supported_error` or `error` to report unsupported cases.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::e: Emits a `GenericConstantTooComplex` error without the `maybe_supported` hint and returns the resulting `ErrorGuaranteed`. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::m: Emits a `GenericConstantTooComplex` error marked as potentially supportable in the future and returns the resulting `ErrorGuaranteed`. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::i: Checks whether a THIR expression is polymorphic by looking for non-region generic parameters in its type, substitutions, or repeat count, treating const params as polymorphic and most other expression kinds as non-polymorphic. For `Repeat`, this method calls `visit_expr`; through that path it also uses the visitor’s `thir` accessor to fetch the repeated subexpression.

Checks whether a THIR pattern is polymorphic by inspecting the pattern type and any constant or range bound values for non-region generic parameters. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.
Returns the underlying THIR being traversed by the polymorphism visitor. It does not call other methods in the Methods List.

Visits an expression during THIR traversal, updates the visitor’s polymorphism flag using `expr_is_poly`, and only continues walking children if no polymorphism has been found yet. This method calls `expr_is_poly`.
Visits a pattern during THIR traversal, updates the visitor’s polymorphism flag using `pat_is_poly`, and stops descending once polymorphism is detected. This method calls `pat_is_poly`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::t: Builds an abstract const for an anonymous or inline const when `generic_const_exprs` is enabled: it fetches the THIR body, runs the `IsThirPolymorphic` visitor to skip monomorphic expressions, and then lowers the root expression into a `ty::Const`. This method calls `recurse_build` after polymorphism checking.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/consts.rs::p: Registers this module’s query providers, wiring `destructure_const` directly and routing abstract-const queries through `thir_abstract_const` with special handling for const arguments. This method calls `thir_abstract_const` from both provider closures.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/abstract_co: Converts an `ErrorGuaranteed` into `NotConstEvaluatable` by wrapping it in the `NotConstEvaluatable::Error` variant; it does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Fetches the optional THIR-derived abstract const for a `WithOptConstParam<DefId>` and wraps the successful result in `EarlyBinder`. It first calls `as_const_arg` to detect const-argument form; if present it calls `thir_abstract_const_of_const_arg`, otherwise it calls `thir_abstract_const`. It then calls `map` on the query result to wrap the abstract const with `EarlyBinder`, returning a `BoundAbstractConst` or propagating query failure.

Expands abstract const references throughout a foldable value by constructing an `Expander` and invoking `fold_with` over the input. During that traversal it uses `Expander::fold_ty` to recurse only into types with const-projection flags, `Expander::fold_const` to replace `ConstKind::Unevaluated` abstract-consts with instantiated THIR abstract const bodies or error consts, and `Expander::interner` as required by the folder interface.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the `Expander`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Folds a type only when it contains const-projection-related flags, avoiding unnecessary traversal for unaffected types. It calls `has_type_flags` to detect whether expansion-relevant flags are present, and calls `super_fold_with` to recursively fold the type when they are.

Expands unevaluated abstract consts during folding by inspecting the const kind, querying for a bound abstract const, converting query errors into const errors, instantiating successful results with region-erased substitutions, and then recursively folding the result. It calls `kind` to inspect the const, `bound_abstract_const` to fetch the abstract const body, `ty` and `const_error_with_guaranteed` to build an error const on failure, `erase_regions` and `subst` to instantiate a retrieved abstract const, and `super_fold_with` to continue recursive folding of the resulting const.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Determines which generic const parameter a local anonymous constant corresponds to by inspecting its HIR parent and surrounding generic argument context, returning `None` when the definition is not an anon const or no matching const parameter can be identified. It calls HIR/navigation helpers such as `hir`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `get`, `parent_id`, and `parent_owner_iter`; lowers unresolved type-relative paths with `ItemCtxt::new` and `ast_ty_to_ty`; inspects projections via `kind`; queries generic parameters with `generics_of`; uses type-checking via `enclosing_body_owner`, `typeck`, and `type_dependent_def_id` for method-call cases; and falls back to diagnostics through `delay_span_bug`, `def_span`, and pattern-path recovery with `get_path_containing_arg_in_pat`.

Walks a pattern tree to find the resolved path whose generic argument list contains the target argument HIR id. It uses a local path-membership check while visiting struct, tuple-struct, and path patterns, and returns the first matching path if found.

Computes `type_of` for local HIR items and returns the result wrapped in an early binder. It directly calls `infer_placeholder_type` for constants whose type was written as `_`, `check_feature_inherent_assoc_ty` when handling inherent associated types, and `type_alias_is_lazy` when deciding how to treat type aliases; it also handles RPITIT cases up front by querying return-position impl-trait information and building the appropriate function, opaque, lowered, or error type for each item kind.

Finds the hidden type for a type-alias `impl Trait` by walking the defining scope, collecting candidate opaque-type constraints from items, impl items, trait items, and closures, and reconciling them into one result. It drives `ConstraintLocator::check` to inspect each potential defining use, relies on the visitor methods `nested_visit_map`, `visit_expr`, `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, and `visit_trait_item` to traverse HIR, and falls back to diagnostics/error types when no consistent constraint is found.

Checks whether a specific local item contributes a constraint for the target opaque type. It calls `has_typeck_results` to skip irrelevant items, `typeck` to read typeck-discovered opaque types, `ty_error` to record tainted error cases, `mir_borrowck` to obtain the concrete hidden type with regions, and `report_mismatch` when a newly found concrete type conflicts with the previously recorded one.
Supplies the HIR map used by the visitor while traversing the defining scope. It calls `hir`.

Visits expressions during opaque-type constraint search, checking closure bodies as potential defining uses before continuing traversal. It calls `check` for `Closure` expressions and then `walk_expr`.
Visits items in the reveal scope, skipping the opaque type item itself, and treats other items as possible sources of hidden-type constraints. It calls `check` on eligible items and then `walk_item`.
Visits impl items in the reveal scope, excluding the opaque type itself, and checks each remaining impl item for hidden-type constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_impl_item`.
Visits trait items and checks each one for constraints on the target opaque type before recursing into it. It calls `check` and then `walk_trait_item`.

Validates the hidden type for a return-position `impl Trait` by taking the owner’s inferred hidden type and then walking the owner body/scope to ensure all nested defining uses agree with it. It drives `ConstraintChecker::check` to compare borrowck-derived opaque types, uses the visitor methods `nested_visit_map`, `visit_expr`, `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, and `visit_trait_item` for traversal, and falls back to `typeck`, `ty_error`, and `mk_diverging_default` when the owner has no usable hidden type.

Checks one local definition for borrowck-produced constraints on the target RPIT opaque type and reports any disagreement with the already chosen hidden type. It calls `mir_borrowck` to inspect concrete opaque types and `report_mismatch` when a non-error mismatch is found.
Supplies the HIR map for the RPIT constraint-checking visitor. It calls `hir`.
Visits expressions while validating RPIT constraints, checking closure bodies as additional defining uses before recursing. It calls `check` for `Closure` expressions and then `walk_expr`.
Visits items in the RPIT reveal scope, skipping the opaque type itself, and validates each remaining item as a potential source of constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_item`.
Visits impl items during RPIT validation, excluding the opaque type itself, and checks each eligible impl item for matching constraints. It calls `check` and then `walk_impl_item`.
Visits trait items during RPIT validation and checks each one for consistency with the chosen hidden type before recursing. It calls `check` and then `walk_trait_item`.

Infers a concrete type for an item declared with a placeholder `_` type by reading the body’s typeck result and improving diagnostics with a concrete suggestion when possible. It calls `bad_placeholder` when no stashed parser diagnostic can be reused, and otherwise emits or updates diagnostics before returning either the inferred type or an error type.

Checks whether the `inherent_associated_types` feature is enabled and emits the corresponding feature-gate error when it is not. This helper performs only the feature validation and diagnostic emission.
Constructs a new `MakeNameable` folder with `success` initialized to `true` and stores the provided `TyCtxt`. This method does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` held by the folder so the `TypeFolder` implementation can access compiler context while folding. This method does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Folds a type into a nameable form when possible: if folding has already failed, it returns the type unchanged; function definitions are converted to function-pointer types; closures and generators mark the transformation as unsuccessful and are left unchanged; all other types are recursively folded. This method explicitly calls `impl<'tcx> TypeFolder<'tcx> for MakeNameable<'tcx>::tcx` indirectly through `self.tcx` access and recursively uses `impl<'tcx> TypeFolder<'tcx> for MakeNameable<'tcx>::fold_ty` via `super_fold_with(self)`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/fn_ctxt/_i: Emits an `UNREACHABLE_CODE` lint when the function context is in `Diverges::Always`, while suppressing noisy lints for certain desugared `if`/`while`/`async`/`await` spans. It updates divergence state to `WarnedAlways` and calls `tcx().node_span_lint` to report the diagnostic.

Resolves inference variables in a type, first returning immediately if no non-region inference remains, then trying a direct resolution, and finally forcing pending obligation selection before resolving again. This method explicitly calls `resolve_vars_if_possible` and `select_obligations_where_possible`.
Records a deferred closure-call resolution by pushing it into the per-closure `deferred_call_resolutions` map.
Removes and returns all deferred call resolutions associated with a closure, yielding an empty vector if none were stored.
Returns a debug tag string containing the `FnCtxt` pointer value.
Looks up the previously recorded type of a local variable from `locals` and crashes with a span bug if the type is missing.

Stores a node type into `typeck_results`, preserving prior `{type error}` entries so later writes do not overwrite them, and tainting the context when an error type is involved. This method explicitly calls `resolve_vars_if_possible`, `tag`, and `set_tainted_by_errors`.
Records the selected field index for a HIR node and, when present, also stores nested field access information in `typeck_results`.
Writes a type-dependent definition resolution result for a HIR node into `typeck_results`.
Stores a canonical user-provided type annotation for a node unless it is the identity form. This method explicitly calls `tag`.

Applies and records expression adjustments, tracks diverging type variables created by `NeverToAny`, detects mutable autoborrows, and composes new adjustments with any existing ones while validating special deref/reborrow cases. This method explicitly calls `convert_place_derefs_to_mutable` when mutable autoderef chains must be upgraded, and uses `dcx().span_delayed_bug` to report invalid adjustment composition.
Fetches predicates for a definition, instantiates them with the given generic arguments, and normalizes the resulting predicates before returning them. This method explicitly calls `normalize`.

Normalizes a foldable value in the current parameter environment and registers any obligations produced by normalization. This method explicitly calls `misc`, `at`, and `register_infer_ok_obligations`.
Adds an obligation requiring a type to satisfy the trait identified by `def_id` at the given cause site. This method explicitly calls `register_bound`.
Requires a type to implement `Sized` unless it already references an error type. This method explicitly calls `require_type_meets` after obtaining the `Sized` lang item with `tcx.require_lang_item`.
Queues a deferred `Sized` obligation for a type unless the type already references an error.
Registers a trait bound obligation with the fulfillment context for a non-error type.
Returns whether a type-like value may contain user lifetime information worth preserving by checking for free regions, aliases, or inference types.

Returns the recorded type for a HIR node, falling back to an error type if the context is already tainted, and otherwise panicking because the node was never assigned a type. This method explicitly calls `tainted_by_errors` and `tag`.
